episodes: Ep 217: Turkey raised its qualified-investor threshold fivefold after a fund rout erased billions in equity value.
Ep 216: Explosions in Riyadh coincide with plans to reopen the airport after recent Houthi strikes.
Ep 215: France deploys 70,000 officers as hundreds of thousands prepare to protest cost-of-living pressures and school conditions for a second weekend.
Ep 214: A White House statement says a ceasefire will open a humanitarian corridor into the besieged Ukrainian town of Oleshky next week.
Ep 213: Russian missiles struck Kyiv hours after a US envoy met Putin, testing any path to talks.
Ep 212: Russia freed a jailed American during US envoy talks with Putin on Ukraine.
Ep 211: South Korea is withdrawing more embassy staff from Ukraine after a prisoner-of-war disclosure dispute.
Ep 210: One million young Britons outside work or training prompt the prime minister to call the situation an economic catastrophe and moral failure.
Ep 209: Czech opposition keeps Senate control, blocking the prime minister from easy constitutional or court changes.
Ep 208: Brazil’s presidential runoff sits in a statistical tie days before voters choose between Lula and Bolsonaro.
Ep 207: G7 nations will run joint drills against AI-driven cyber attacks that could hit power grids, banks and hospitals across member countries.
Ep 206: European Union leaders meet to address a €360 billion trade deficit with China while setting the bloc’s next seven-year budget and Ukraine support.
Ep 205: A bridge between China and North Korea that sat unused for 12 years will open this week, shifting trade routes in Northeast Asia.
Ep 204: China and Russia are aligning maritime strategies to protect energy shipping lanes that supply both economies.
Ep 203: Singapore activates medical subsidies as regional fires push it to the world's most polluted city ranking.
Ep 202: Panama declares a state of emergency after two major earthquakes damage buildings across every province.
Ep 201: Taiwan sets a record defence budget to deter war with China, affecting security for its 23 million residents.
Ep 200: US Treasury Secretary may skip a regional finance meeting to prepare for talks with Chinese officials on extending a bilateral trade truce.
Ep 199: Taiwan's top chipmaker posted a 55 percent sales jump last month as demand for AI chips keeps rising.
Ep 198: North Korea’s warning to the US over Taiwan arms deliveries shows its tightening alignment with Russia, raising risks for East Asian security.
Ep 197: Quebec’s new separatist government has pledged an independence referendum despite winning only a minority of seats.
Ep 196: Yemen’s government has launched a major offensive against Houthi-held territory, testing whether outside powers can contain the fighting’s spread into key shipping lanes.
Ep 195: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz reached Kyiv with plans for one billion euros in new military aid and joint drone production.
Ep 194: Latvia holds a parliamentary election today as voters weigh national security against rising living costs in the NATO member that borders Russia.
Ep 193: Skydance will control Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery, two studios releasing 35 films next year.
Ep 192: A $16bn Kenyan oil refinery breaks ground to boost East African industry, despite protests over land compensation from locals.
Ep 191: A US-China summit produced no public shift on Taiwan, leaving the island's security arrangements in the same uncertain state for the coming year.
Ep 190: US forces will leave their final Iraq bases by Wednesday, ending a two-decade military presence in a country where 4,500 Americans died.
Ep 189: SpaceX will attempt the first orbital flight of its Starship rocket today, a test that could open new routes for satellites and future crewed missions beyond Earth orbit.
Ep 188: Venezuela has released 39 political prisoners after a second round of talks between its interim government and opposition.
Ep 187: US and Japanese finance ministers met to address yen concerns raised by President Trump at their summit.
Ep 186: US and China extend trade truce to January, giving supply chains temporary relief from tariff uncertainty.
Ep 185: Pakistan's air strikes on Afghan sites test mediation efforts that could affect stability across South Asia.
Ep 184: Rescuers search for thousands missing in Nepal's floods as aid cuts raise risks for millions in the Himalayas.
Ep 183: A South Korean court has reduced the prison term for the country's former first lady to five years, a decision that tests how judicial systems weigh accountability for those close to power.
Ep 182: Pakistan’s airstrikes on Afghan civilian areas have killed three people and raised the risk of renewed border fighting between the two neighbors.
Ep 181: China is rejecting calls to slow its AI development just weeks before a planned summit with the United States.
Ep 180: A new U.S. military arrangement in Greenland could reshape Arctic security arrangements involving Denmark and NATO partners.
Ep 179: Taiwan ran its first joint military exercise with multiple attack drones, showing how the island is updating its defenses amid regional tensions.
Ep 178: The US House has passed a broad sanctions package on Russia and sent it to the president, tightening economic pressure on Moscow.

Ep 177: Congress has voted for a third time to limit presidential military action in Iran, testing the balance between executive power and legislative oversight on a conflict affecting regional stability.
Ep 176: Canada is deepening ties with Europe as frictions with the United States grow, while a U.K. hospital inquiry highlights systemic failures and global debates over AI rules continue.
Ep 175: Central banks in the world’s two largest economies face fresh market pressure on interest rates this week, shaping borrowing costs for households and businesses across continents.
Ep 174: An international tribunal has ruled that India should not have suspended a 65-year-old water-sharing treaty with Pakistan, raising stakes for 300 million people who rely on the rivers.
Ep 173: BRICS leaders gather in New Delhi this weekend while wars in Ukraine and the Middle East test whether the group can coordinate responses to U.S. pressure and ongoing regional conflicts.
Ep 172: Oil crossing $100 a barrel raises fuel and goods costs for households and businesses across import-dependent economies.
Ep 171: A pledge of $5,000 payments to every American adult if Republicans win the midterms raises questions about trillion-dollar spending and congressional approval.
Ep 170: Bangladesh is fighting the world's worst measles outbreak, driven by vaccination gaps that leave millions of children vulnerable as health systems work to contain the spread.
Ep 169: China's exports rose 25 percent last month, pushing its annual trade surplus past $800 billion and shifting pressure on global supply chains.
Ep 168: The United States and China are exploring direct talks on AI safety rules even as their technology competition intensifies.
Ep 167: Clashes between US and Iranian forces near the Strait of Hormuz have intensified with new strikes on tankers and a drone, directly affecting oil transit routes used by millions worldwide.
Ep 166: US envoys head to Moscow and Kyiv carrying a fresh plan to end the war in Ukraine, a conflict that has already reshaped European security and global energy markets.
Ep 165: Argentina’s sanctions on unauthorized oil exploration near the Falklands test Britain’s position and Washington’s shifting neutrality in a decades-old sovereignty dispute.
Ep 164: A last-minute U.S. funding bill signed by the president keeps federal operations running through the midterms, easing immediate pressure on government services and markets.
Ep 163: Renewed US and Iranian strikes have ended a lull in their conflict, raising immediate risks for energy supplies and stability across the Middle East.
Ep 162: India's exam system for secure government jobs has sparked huge protests because years of preparation often lead nowhere for millions of young people.
Ep 161: US strikes on an Iranian island killed two and injured two, the first direct action in weeks, testing whether regional tensions will widen.
Ep 160: Leaders from Russia, China, India and Iran meet in Central Asia this week to deepen ties while facing Western sanctions and trade pressure.
Ep 159: The United States has reached a deal to access Venezuela’s 65 billion barrels of oil reserves, a move that could reshape energy flows for major economies.
Ep 158: A federal judge has blocked President Trump’s executive order on mail voting, leaving ballot rules for millions of Americans unsettled ahead of future elections.
Ep 157: Updated COVID vaccines cleared for the coming season give health systems a fresh tool to protect millions as respiratory illness patterns shift.
Ep 156: Iran is preparing to charge fees for ships passing the Strait of Hormuz, a route that carries roughly one-fifth of global oil trade.
Ep 155: Canada’s new tariffs on U.S. goods raise the cost of everyday items for households on both sides of the border while testing the next phase of trade talks.
Ep 154: Institutions that underpin prosperity in wealthy nations face mounting pressure, with one Nobel economist arguing the working class must be central to any fix.
Ep 153: Alibaba’s $10 billion share sale to fund AI has cut its stock price, showing how heavy tech spending now shapes investor returns across Asia.
Ep 152: Oil supplies are tightening worldwide as the Hormuz passage remains contested, pushing up energy costs for households and industries.
Ep 151: The United States has placed 50 percent tariffs on roughly 20 billion dollars of Canadian goods after trade talks collapsed, and Canada has said it will respond with matching duties.
Ep 150: The Panama Canal will limit daily ship passages from September because of drought, raising costs on routes that carry roughly 5 percent of global trade.
Ep 149: A Missouri judge has cleared Trump-backed U.S. House districts for November use, locking in the map that will shape control of Congress for millions of voters.
Ep 148: A former Ukrainian defense minister’s call for elections tests how long martial law can suspend normal democratic processes during an active war.
Ep 147: Brazilian lawmakers are expanding their influence over the executive branch while many other democracies see the opposite shift.

Ep 146: U.S. President Trump has ordered cuts to joint military drills with South Korea, citing costs and his relationship with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, a shift that could alter deterrence calculations on the peninsula.
Ep 145: North Korea’s reported plan to send up to 50,000 troops to support Russia’s war in Ukraine could alter the conflict’s manpower balance and test alliances across Asia and Europe.
Ep 144: South Korea’s president is pushing to replace the 1953 armistice with a formal peace treaty, a step that could reshape security arrangements across East Asia.

Ep 143: A UK by-election boycotted by major parties delivered a seat to Reform UK while a comedian captured over a quarter of votes, showing how protest options can shape local outcomes when turnout is low.
Ep 142: India’s planned coal mining expansion now leads the world, directly shaping how much fossil fuel will be available for power generation in coming years.
Ep 141: Renewed fighting around Iran is widening the global oil supply gap faster than expected, which could push energy prices higher for households and industries everywhere.
Ep 140: The Strait of Hormuz stays shut, keeping one-fifth of global oil trade off the market until Iran and the United States resolve their standoff over blockades and sanctions.
Ep 139: Ukraine’s strikes on Russian oil facilities tighten pressure on Moscow’s energy supplies while winter demand looms.
Ep 138: A new U.S. tariff on a key solar material raises costs for clean-energy supply chains that serve millions of households and businesses.
Ep 137: The US Senate has approved new sanctions on Russia aimed at strengthening support for Ukraine, tightening economic pressure on Moscow.
Ep 136: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan are preparing a joint defence agreement that could alter security calculations across a region already under strain from multiple conflicts.
Ep 135: Ukraine’s targeted strikes on Russian oil refineries threaten energy flows that millions across Europe depend on for fuel and power.
Ep 134: Record electricity demand from China's heatwave is testing northern power grids that supply millions of homes and factories.
Ep 133: Thailand’s prime minister is seeking measured talks with Myanmar’s military rulers, a move that could shape stability and refugee flows across Southeast Asia.
Ep 132: Coordinated US-Japan action has lifted the yen, easing import costs for Japanese households while signaling closer currency coordination between the world's largest economies.
Ep 131: US President Trump has canceled a planned strike on Iran after outlining terms for a deal, reducing the immediate risk of wider conflict in the Middle East.
Ep 130: Taiwan’s economy expanded nearly 13 percent in the second quarter, driven by AI demand and closer U.S. links that are reshaping supply chains across the region.
Ep 129: China's factory slowdown raises questions about demand across Asia and beyond, with ripple effects on jobs and trade.
Ep 128: American public opposition to the Iran conflict is now clear in fresh polling, narrowing the room for sustained U.S. military action.
Ep 127: Russia charges Telegram’s founder with aiding terrorism and issues an international arrest warrant, raising questions about platform liability worldwide.
Ep 126: US states now shoulder rising costs for food assistance, creating direct pressure to trim recipient rolls.
Ep 125: Surging profits at Chinese chipmakers signal how AI demand is reshaping global technology supply chains and national industrial strategies.
Ep 124: A looming super El Nino could cost African countries up to $20 billion and drive mass migration from drought-hit regions.
Ep 123: Saudi Arabia’s strike on Yemen’s main port raises the risk of wider disruption to Red Sea shipping that carries fuel and goods for millions across the Middle East and beyond.
Ep 122: New U.S. tariffs of 10-12.5% on imports from 60 countries will raise costs for many goods and affect trade worldwide.
Ep 121: The United States has signed a landmark nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia, reshaping energy ties and non-proliferation rules across the Middle East.
Ep 120: Ukraine names a new army chief as shipping firms add fees over Hormuz risks and UK inflation eases to 2.6 percent.
Ep 119: U.S. tariffs on Canadian goods and a major rescue in India show how trade policy and industrial accidents reshape daily costs and safety for millions.
Ep 118: A cyberattack on a major Japanese frozen-food supplier has forced KFC outlets to warn of shortages, showing how one breach can ripple through daily supply chains for millions of customers.
Ep 117: Two U.S. soldiers killed in Jordan mark the first American deaths since renewed Iran fighting, raising stakes for Middle East stability and global shipping routes.
Ep 116: Venezuela's twin earthquakes have killed more than 5,000 people and now require coordinated international reconstruction aid to begin.

Ep 115: A Ukrainian tycoon's accusation that Kyiv's intelligence service tried to assassinate him in Monaco highlights deepening internal fractures that could affect the country's war effort and Western support.
Ep 114: Tens of thousands remain missing after twin earthquakes struck Venezuela’s coast, with rescue efforts stalled weeks later by absent government aid.
Ep 113: Proposals to raise the UK state pension age sooner would force millions to work longer before claiming benefits, tightening public finances amid demographic pressures.
Ep 112: Sam Neill’s death at 78 closes a chapter for generations who grew up with Jurassic Park and The Piano, underscoring how individual careers shape shared cultural memory across decades.
Ep 111: A British tourist's death on an Ibiza hotel waterslide and a Yellowstone bison attack on a visitor highlight everyday safety risks at popular leisure spots.

Ep 110: Senator Lindsey Graham’s sudden death removes a central figure in US foreign policy just as American strikes on Iran trigger missile and drone attacks on Gulf states and a threatened closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
Ep 109: US-Iran talks over safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz now shape global fuel costs and shipping reliability for households and businesses worldwide.
Ep 108: Deadly wildfires in southern Spain have killed at least 11 people during record heat, underscoring immediate dangers to residents and travelers in affected regions.
Ep 107: A man has denied attempting to murder ten people after a stabbing attack on a UK train, prompting fresh scrutiny of passenger safety measures.
Ep 106: The collapse of the US-Iran ceasefire raises immediate risks to global energy supplies and Middle East stability as strikes resume.
Ep 105: NATO allies convene in Ankara as defense spending debates and regional security concerns shape outcomes for member nations facing shifting global threats.
Ep 104: Russia's intensified strikes on Kyiv have killed 18 and exposed Ukraine's shrinking stock of interceptor missiles, directly affecting civilian safety and NATO planning.
Ep 103: Trump's offer to mediate the Ukraine war in a 90-minute call with Putin raises the prospect of renewed high-level diplomacy just before a NATO summit.
Ep 102: Iran's supreme leader's death has drawn millions to Tehran amid anti-American chants, raising questions about succession and regional stability after 36 years of his rule.
Ep 101: At least 32 people died when an overcrowded bus plunged into a ravine in Pakistan, underscoring the lethal risks of long-distance travel on steep mountain roads.
Ep 100: Lithuania's move to end its nuclear weapons ban signals a broader European shift toward stronger deterrence as Russia’s neighbors reassess long-standing restrictions.
Ep 99: Breakdown in U.S.-Iran talks is pushing oil prices higher, raising costs for drivers and heating bills worldwide while clouding prospects for regional stability.
Ep 98: Twin earthquakes have flattened parts of Venezuela, leaving residents without news of loved ones and testing the country's capacity to deliver emergency aid.
Ep 97: A mass shooting near a German youth centre has killed five people, triggering immediate area lockdowns and fresh scrutiny of public safety measures.
Ep 96: The week's biggest developments, pulled together — what actually moved, why it matters, and what to watch next.
Ep 95: US strikes on Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz risk collapsing a 60-day ceasefire and derailing ongoing talks between Washington and Tehran.
Ep 94: The Iran conflict is cutting Heathrow passenger numbers and profits, raising costs and uncertainty for UK travelers and the wider aviation sector.
